#!/usr/bin/env bash
# THE caos stack (design/one-stack-image.md): start the daemon group, wait
# until it is serving, then supervise it. This is the one bring-up in the
# tree — `caosd serve` is this script, and every placement runs it:
#
#   test   the stack image's /worker starts it, runs worker1 against it,
#          and stops it (test-stack/worker)
#   host   `caosd up` runs the stack image with this as its command
#   seed   the flake's seed derivation runs it to publish std
#
# The container is the CALLER's decision, not this script's. It configures
# itself from the environment and nothing else, so it is correct wherever it
# is put — which is the whole point: there is no second bring-up to drift
# against.
#
# DIES AS A GROUP. A half-dead stack is not something anyone should have to
# diagnose, so any member's death takes the rest down and exits non-zero.
# Callers that need to keep working (the test placement) run this in the
# background and watch both the ready file and this process.
#
# Configuration, all environment:
#   CAOS_STACK_STATE   dir holding the server's git repo (required)
#   CAOS_STACK_LOGS    dir for <member>.log (required)
#   CAOS_STACK_READY   file to touch once every member is serving (optional)
#   CAOS_STACK_BIN     dir holding `server` and `runnerd` (required)
#   CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT     redis port (required)
#   CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PERSIST  "yes" for an appendonly cache, "no" to keep it
#                             in memory and lose it with the process
#   CAOS_STACK_REGISTRY       "yes" to run a registry in the group, "no" to use
#                             someone else's. The host placement runs one; the
#                             test placement deliberately does not — a
#                             content-addressed registry shared across tests
#                             cannot leak behaviour, only work, and sharing it
#                             is what stops every test rebaking the toolchain.
#   CAOS_STACK_RUNNERD        "yes" to run runnerd, "no" for a placement that
#                             dispatches no jobs. The seed is the "no": it only
#                             PUBLISHES, and build-builtins.sh runs no workers,
#                             which is what makes the seed legal inside the
#                             flake-builder container (it holds no engine socket
#                             grant, and does not need one).
#   CAOS_STACK_SEED_GIT       optional: a prebuilt server repo to start from.
#                             std published at image build time rides in the
#                             image as one of these (design/one-stack-image.md,
#                             "The seed"), so a fresh stack has std without
#                             publishing it.
#   CAOS_RUNNER_SLOTS         runnerd's concurrency
#   CAOS_PENDING_TIMEOUT_SECS how long a job waits for a runner to exist
#
# Passed through to runnerd untouched, because they are the caller's business:
# DOCKER_HOST (which engine), CAOS_DOCKER_NETWORK (which netns workers join),
# CAOS_RUNNER_SOCKET (the socket this pool MAY grant, per-image).
set -euo pipefail

: "${CAOS_STACK_STATE:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_STATE}"
: "${CAOS_STACK_LOGS:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_LOGS}"
: "${CAOS_STACK_BIN:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_BIN}"
: "${CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT}"
: "${CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PERSIST:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PERSIST (yes|no)}"
: "${CAOS_STACK_REGISTRY:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_REGISTRY (yes|no)}"
: "${CAOS_STACK_RUNNERD:?serve needs CAOS_STACK_RUNNERD (yes|no)}"

# The server self-bootstraps an empty repo on first boot, but the directory
# has to be there for it to bootstrap into.
mkdir -p "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/git" "$CAOS_STACK_LOGS"

# A seeded repo, if this placement ships one: the test stack's std is
# published once per tree, at image build time, rather than once per test
# (design/one-stack-image.md, "The seed"). HEAD is the probe because that is
# what the server's own `gix::open` check turns on — no HEAD, no repo — and
# only an ABSENT repo is seeded: a persistent stack's own is the newer truth.
#
# `cp -RL`, and the L is load-bearing. An image built by dockerTools lays its
# contents down as an lndir SYMLINK FARM, so every file here is a link into
# /nix/store. Copying those verbatim gives a repo whose HEAD is a symlink, and
# git's validate_headref only accepts a symlinked HEAD when the target starts
# with `refs/` — so `git -C <dir> config` reports "not in a git directory" and
# every request answers "Not a git repository", while gix opens it happily and
# the server comes up anyway. Dereference, and the copy is real files the
# server can also write to (hence the chmod: the store is read-only).
if [ -n "${CAOS_STACK_SEED_GIT:-}" ] && [ ! -e "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/git/HEAD" ]; then
  echo "caosd serve: seeding the server repo from $CAOS_STACK_SEED_GIT" >&2
  cp -RL "$CAOS_STACK_SEED_GIT/." "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/git/"
  chmod -R u+w "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/git"
fi

# The server always listens on :80 and always reaches redis on loopback: every
# placement puts the group in one netns, so there is no address to negotiate.
# Workers join that same netns (CAOS_DOCKER_NETWORK), which is why they can
# use this URL verbatim.
SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1
REDIS_ADDR=127.0.0.1:$CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT

pids=()
names=()

fail() {
  echo "caosd serve: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

# A REQUESTED shutdown, as opposed to a member dying: take the group down and
# exit 0. Without this, killing serve orphans redis and the server — they are
# children of this shell, not of its caller — and the seed derivation would
# copy a git dir still open by a live server.
shutdown() {
  kill "${pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 0
}
trap shutdown TERM INT

# Start a member, remember it, and name it for the supervisor's diagnostics.
start() { # <name> <command...>
  local name=$1
  shift
  "$@" >"$CAOS_STACK_LOGS/$name.log" 2>&1 &
  pids+=("$!")
  names+=("$name")
}

# --- redis: the result cache -------------------------------------------------
redis_args=(--port "$CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT")
if [ "$CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PERSIST" = yes ]; then
  # appendonly keeps it durable to a hard kill, not just a clean shutdown-save.
  redis_args+=(--dir "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/redis" --appendonly yes)
  mkdir -p "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/redis"
else
  # No persistence: the cache starts empty and dies with this process. The
  # incrementality tests assert real memoization, so a cache that outlives a
  # test's stack would poison them.
  redis_args+=(--save '')
fi
start redis redis-server "${redis_args[@]}"
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  redis-cli -p "$CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 0.5
done
redis-cli -p "$CAOS_STACK_REDIS_PORT" ping >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "redis never came up"

# --- registry: the image cache, when this placement owns one -----------------
if [ "$CAOS_STACK_REGISTRY" = yes ]; then
  mkdir -p "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/registry"
  cat > "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/registry.yml" <<YML
version: 0.1
storage:
  filesystem:
    rootdirectory: $CAOS_STACK_STATE/registry
http:
  addr: :5000
YML
  start registry registry serve "$CAOS_STACK_STATE/registry.yml"
  ok=""
  for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
    # -s, not -sS: every attempt before the registry is listening would
    # otherwise print a connection error, and a retry loop's noise reads like
    # a failure in the logs the FIRST real failure dumps.
    if curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:5000/v2/"; then ok=1; break; fi
    sleep 1
  done
  [ -n "$ok" ] || fail "registry never came up"
fi

# --- server ------------------------------------------------------------------
start server env \
  CAOS_GIT_DIR="$CAOS_STACK_STATE/git" \
  CAOS_REDIS_ADDR="$REDIS_ADDR" \
  CAOS_PENDING_TIMEOUT_SECS="${CAOS_PENDING_TIMEOUT_SECS:-900}" \
  "$CAOS_STACK_BIN/server"
ok=""
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  if git ls-remote "$SERVER_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=1; break; fi
  sleep 1
done
[ -n "$ok" ] || fail "server never came up"

# --- runnerd: the compute half, when this placement dispatches jobs ----------
# runnerd hands its OWN CAOS_SERVER_URL to every worker it launches
# (crates/runnerd/src/main.rs). Where workers share this netns — the test
# placement, `container:<self>` — loopback is right for both. On the host they
# get their own netns on a bridge, so runnerd must advertise a name that
# resolves there; it also resolves from in here, via the stack's alias.
if [ "$CAOS_STACK_RUNNERD" = yes ]; then
  start runnerd env \
    CAOS_SERVER_URL="${CAOS_STACK_RUNNER_SERVER_URL:-$SERVER_URL}" \
    CAOS_DOCKER_BIN="${CAOS_DOCKER_BIN:-docker}" \
    CAOS_RUNNER_SLOTS="${CAOS_RUNNER_SLOTS:-8}" \
    "$CAOS_STACK_BIN/runnerd"
  sleep 1
  grep -q "slots, server" "$CAOS_STACK_LOGS/runnerd.log" \
    || fail "runnerd did not start"
fi

# Not `[ ... ] && ...`: under `set -e` a false test would make that list the
# script's last status and exit 0 right here, silently skipping the supervisor.
if [ -n "${CAOS_STACK_READY:-}" ]; then
  : > "$CAOS_STACK_READY"
fi
echo "caosd serve: ${names[*]} up on $SERVER_URL" >&2

# --- supervise ---------------------------------------------------------------
# `wait -n` returns when the FIRST member exits — which, since none of them is
# supposed to exit, always means something is wrong. Name it, take the rest
# down, and fail.
wait -n
for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do
  kill -0 "${pids[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || dead=${names[$i]}
done
kill "${pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true
wait 2>/dev/null || true
fail "${dead:-a member} exited — the stack is down (see $CAOS_STACK_LOGS)"
